```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a figure
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


**NRES 746, Week 7, Lecture 1: Reading the Interval**


**Instructions:** Work alone on Part 1 (about 4 minutes), then compare
with a neighbor for Part 2. Keep laptops closed.

## The data

You swab 20 frogs from a pond for chytrid fungus, and 2 test positive.
Model the number of positives as binomial with unknown prevalence $p$.
The figure shows the negative log-likelihood (NLL) for these data,
minus its minimum value (so the lowest point of the curve is at zero).

```{r chytrid-nll, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.4}
p_grid <- seq(0.001, 0.4, by = 0.001)
nll <- -dbinom(2, size = 20, prob = p_grid, log = TRUE)
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 0.4), ylim = c(0, 5), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     xlab = "Prevalence, p", ylab = "NLL minus its minimum", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.1))
axis(1, at = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.02), labels = FALSE, tcl = -0.25)
abline(v = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.02), h = seq(0, 5, by = 0.5), col = "grey85")
lines(p_grid, nll - min(nll), lwd = 2)
box()
```

```{r key-values, include=FALSE}
f2 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 2)
# range of p with NLL within 2 units of its minimum
within2 <- function(k, n) {
  f <- function(p) -dbinom(k, n, p, log = TRUE) + dbinom(k, n, k / n, log = TRUE) - 2
  c(uniroot(f, c(1e-6, k / n))$root, uniroot(f, c(k / n, 0.99))$root)
}
ci20 <- within2(2, 20)
ci80 <- within2(8, 80)
```


## Part 1: Read the curve (individual)

**1a.** What is the maximum likelihood estimate of $p$?

$\hat{p} \approx$ \ans{0.10}


**1b.** A common rule of thumb treats every value of $p$ whose NLL is
within 2 units of the minimum as plausible. Draw that cutoff on
the figure, then read off the approximate range of plausible values.

From \ans{`r f2(ci20[1])`} to \ans{`r f2(ci20[2])`}


**1c.** Is this range *symmetric* around $\hat{p}$? Why might the curve
be lopsided for these data?

\ans{No: it stretches farther above 0.10 than below. With only 2 positives the curve is squeezed against $p = 0$ (prevalence can't be negative), so it rises steeply on the left and slowly on the right.}


## Part 2: More frogs (with a neighbor)

**2a.** A second survey swabs 80 frogs and finds 8 positive. Sketch its
curve on the same figure. Will its range of plausible values be wider
or narrower than yours, and does $\hat{p}$ change? Compare sketches
with your neighbor.

\ans{Narrower (about `r f2(ci80[1])` to `r f2(ci80[2])`); $\hat p$ stays at 0.10. Four times the data makes the curve much steeper and less lopsided.}

```{r ans-curves, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.4}
nll80 <- -dbinom(8, size = 80, prob = p_grid, log = TRUE)
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 0.4), ylim = c(0, 5), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     xlab = "Prevalence, p", ylab = "NLL minus its minimum", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.1))
abline(v = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.02), h = seq(0, 5, by = 0.5), col = "grey85")
lines(p_grid, nll - min(nll), lwd = 2)
lines(p_grid, nll80 - min(nll80), lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = ans_col)
abline(h = 2, col = ans_col, lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright", c("2 of 20", "8 of 80", "cutoff (2 units)"), lwd = 2,
       lty = c(1, 2, 1), col = c("black", ans_col, ans_col), bty = "n")
box()
```
